sections.h2: How can I sell a house in Teaneck?
sections.html:
Teaneck owners choose between listing with an agent, selling privately, and accepting an as-is offer from a cash buyer. Teaneck is a dense, close-in suburb, so a conventional listing draws plenty of attention, while a direct sale suits an owner facing an inherited property, tenants, deferred repairs or a tight deadline.

Whatever the route, the township has two checks to clear before closing: the Fire Prevention Bureau's resale inspection for smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers, and a clean record with the Building Department. Start both early. A house with an open permit or a missing detector can slow a closing whether the buyer is financing or paying cash.

sections.h2: What kind of township is Teaneck?
sections.html:
Teaneck is a Bergen County township of 6.24 square miles, 6.04 of them land, with 41,246 residents at the 2020 Census and a density of about 6,800 people per square mile. That made it the second most populous of Bergen County's 70 municipalities, behind Hackensack. It borders River Edge and Hackensack across the Hackensack River, New Milford and Bergenfield to the north, Englewood and Leonia to the east, and Ridgefield Park and Bogota to the south.

Route 4 divides the township into northern and southern halves, and the CSX River Subdivision rail line divides it east from west. Shopping and services cluster in four districts:

  • Cedar Lane, which had a $3.9 million streetscape project completed in 2006
  • North Teaneck Road
  • West Englewood Avenue and Queen Anne Road, known as The Plaza
  • Queen Anne Road and DeGraw Avenue

The township also keeps 24 municipal parks, 14 of them developed.

sections.h2: How did Teaneck develop, and which houses are historic?
sections.html:
Teaneck was created on February 19, 1895, from parts of Englewood and Ridgefield townships and Bogota. It chose the township form of government at a time when most new Bergen County communities were becoming boroughs. Early settlement followed Teaneck Road and River Road, where several Dutch stone houses from the 1700s still stand and some are on the National Register of Historic Places.

The big change came when the Phelps Estate opened for development in 1927 and the George Washington Bridge opened in 1931, tying the town to Manhattan by way of Route 4. The population nearly quadrupled between 1920 and 1930, from 4,192 to 16,513. The United States Army named Teaneck a model community in 1949, and in 1965 the township voluntarily integrated its public schools. A second major wave of building followed World War II, so many Teaneck houses are decades old, and older wiring, heating and permit gaps are the items to check before you list.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Teaneck?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts the population at 43,329 for July 2025, a 5.0% increase from the 2020 base. Of 13,716 households, 77.5% are owner-occupied, and the typical household has 3.00 people, larger than the national figure of 2.53. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $546,100, median gross rent is $1,832, and median household income is $144,075. Workers spend an average of 34.4 minutes getting to their jobs.

More than a quarter of residents (27.1%) were born outside the country, 37.2% of people age 5 and older speak a language other than English at home, and 57.2% of adults 25 and older have a bachelor's degree or higher. Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts.

sections.h2: What does Teaneck require when a home is resold?
sections.html:
The Fire Prevention Bureau states that every residence is inspected upon resale, under state law, for required smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers. The bureau's number is (201) 837-1600, extension 5206. Fix any missing device before you book, because a failed inspection means a second visit.

For the structure itself, Teaneck follows the state construction code. On the owner's request, the construction official can issue a certificate of continued occupancy for an existing building when no violations or orders are pending and records show the use has lawfully existed. That certificate reflects a general inspection of the visible parts of the building and confirms that no unsafe conditions were found. Teaneck's page for certificates of occupancy cites N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.23 and points owners to the Building Department for the application.

Before listing a house with a deck, pool, shed, driveway or fence, find out whether the work had a zoning permit. The township requires an accurate survey drawn to scale by a New Jersey licensed surveyor with a zoning application, and its zoning staff check the survey on site. The Building Department's number for zoning application status is (201) 837-1600, extension 1100.

sections.h2: Which roads and transit options do Teaneck buyers use?
sections.html:
Teaneck sits where Interstate 95, the New Jersey Turnpike, meets the eastern end of Interstate 80, so highway access is a main selling point. The table summarizes the principal roads.

RoadRole in Teaneck
Route 42.5 miles east to west from Hackensack to Englewood; leads to the George Washington Bridge; rush-hour backups where it narrows between Belle Avenue and Englewood
Interstate 951.3 miles through the township from Ridgefield Park to Leonia
Interstate 80Eastern terminus at the I-95 junction; the last 0.9 miles run from Bogota
County roadsTeaneck Road, Queen Anne Road, River Road, Fort Lee Road and Cedar Lane

Source: Teaneck, New Jersey (Wikipedia). NJ Transit buses serve Teaneck Road, Route 4 and Cedar Lane toward the Port Authority Bus Terminal and the George Washington Bridge Bus Station, so check NJ Transit for current route numbers. The township has no passenger train service of its own. Riders use the New Bridge Landing station in River Edge or the Anderson Street station in Hackensack, both on the Pascack Valley Line to Hoboken. Newark Liberty is about 20 miles away, and Teterboro Airport is 9 miles away.

sections.h2: Which schools, hospitals and employers shape demand in Teaneck?
sections.html:
Teaneck Public Schools serves pre-kindergarten through grade 12 in eight schools and enrolled 3,487 students in 2023-24. The schools are Bryant, Theodora Smiley Lacey, Hawthorne, Lowell and Whittier for the early grades, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson middle schools, and Teaneck High School with 1,261 students. Teaneck Community Charter School is a separate public charter school, and Bergen County Technical Schools, including the Bergen County Academies in Hackensack, accept students by application.

Holy Name Medical Center and the Metropolitan Campus of Fairleigh Dickinson University are major institutions. Cognizant keeps its global headquarters at the Glenpointe Centre, which includes a 350-room hotel and 650,000 square feet of office space, and Phibro Animal Health is based at the I-95 and I-80 junction. Local employment gives some buyers a short commute.

sections.h2: What parks and open space does Teaneck offer?
sections.html: Votee Park is the largest, at 40.51 acres, with ball fields, playgrounds, the township pool and a Sportsplex that opened in 2014. The 3.5-mile Hackensack River Greenway through Teaneck became a National Recreation Trail in June 2009. Overpeck County Park, more than 800 acres along Overpeck Creek, is shared with neighboring municipalities, and the Teaneck Creek Conservancy maintains 1.3 miles of trails near the Interstates. Photograph a park or greenway within walking distance, because buyers often ask how close one is.

sections.h2: What state forms and fees apply at a Teaneck closing?
sections.html:
The seller pays New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded, calculated on the price in the deed. For a price over $350,000 the rate rises in steps per $500 of consideration, and sales above $1,000,000 add a graduated fee that begins at 1%. The Division of Taxation publishes the rate tables on its realty transfer fee page.

The seller also signs a GIT/REP form, which tells the county clerk whether a nonresident must prepay Gross Income Tax. Your attorney or title company will handle both filings. Ask the Teaneck tax collector for your current balance and any sewer or other municipal charges before the closing date.

faqs.q: Does Teaneck inspect a house when it is sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The Fire Prevention Bureau says all residences are inspected upon resale under state law for smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers. Call (201) 837-1600, extension 5206, to ask about scheduling.

faqs.q: What is a certificate of continued occupancy in Teaneck?
faqs.a: It is a certificate for an existing building that the construction official can issue on the owner's request. It states that a general inspection of the visible parts found no violations of the state rules and no unsafe conditions, and that the use has lawfully existed.

faqs.q: Is Teaneck a good market for a fast sale?
faqs.a: Teaneck has 77.5% owner-occupied housing, a median home value of $546,100 and a population that grew 5.0% since 2020, so buyer interest is steady. A fast sale still depends on the house's condition, permit record and price.

faqs.q: Which office should I call about a zoning permit?
faqs.a: Call the Building Department at (201) 837-1600, extension 1100, with your Zoning Control Number to check an application. Incomplete applications are not accepted, and the application must include an accurate survey.

faqs.q: Who pays the realty transfer fee in Teaneck?
faqs.a: The seller pays it, through the closing agent, when the deed is recorded. The amount depends on the price in the deed, and New Jersey publishes the rate tables and exemptions.
